hello.text: Hello, little one. I'm getting water from the well.

bridge.text: Listen to the river splashing along! I'm glad we have a strong bridge, so we can all visit each other.

beans.text: Miss Miriam tells me you planted beans with her. When they come in, maybe we'll all share a supper.

bread.text: Was it you who filled our bread basket? Two rolls, one for me and one for my husband. Thank you, little one.

sheep_wonder.text: When I was little, my grandma had sheep. She knew all their names. If one got lost, she looked until she found it. Then she sang all the way home.

shepherd_wonder.text: When I was little and couldn't sleep, my mother would sit by me and say, "The Lord is my shepherd." I still say it at night.

lambs_fed.text: You fed my lambs! Every trough had the same, so nobody went hungry. Thank you, little one.

lambs_offer.text: You came! Thank you for reading my letter. The lambs are so hungry. Would you please help me share out their hay?

choices.text: Yes, please! I'd be glad to.

lambs_go.text: Wonderful. Come and stand by the troughs with me.

lambs_later.text: That's all right. The lambs and I will be here.

card_give.text: Hello, little one! What's that you're holding so carefully?
card_give.reply: This card is for you, Mrs. Ruth. Thank you for being so kind to us.

card_thanks.text: For me? Oh, look at the little flowers, and a heart! Thank you, my dear. I'll put it by my window, where I can see it every day.

pond_offer.text: You came! Look, the dipping net is full. Would you like to help me sort what we've found?

pond_go.text: Wonderful. Gently, now. They're small, and they're God's creatures too.

pond_later.text: That's all right. The pond isn't going anywhere.

pond_thanks.text: Every little creature back in its home. You were so gentle with them.
